title: Learner resource bounds
statement: Let $n$, $a$, $b$, and $s$ be natural numbers with $0<n$, $0<a$, $2a\le b$, and $1\le s$. For every target function $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, the deterministic Goldreich–Levin learner with dimension $n$, accuracy parameter $a/b$, and Fourier bound $s$ uses zero random examples, makes at most its specified query budget, and performs at most its specified work budget.
hypotheses_covered: Twice the accuracy numerator is at most its denominator
The Fourier bound is at least one
The target is a function from the sign cube of dimension n to the signs
